description: JUSTIFICATION FOR EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY Project Name: West Valley Development Project (WVDP) Technical Assistance Contract (TAC) Estimated Cost/Price of the Task Order: Approximately $5M Authority: FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C) Type Determination: Individual I. Contracting Activity United States Department of Energy, Environmental Management Consolidated Business Center (EMCBC), Office of Contracting, Contracting Officer, Jennifer K. M. Splitt. II. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Processed The EMCBC is proposing to issue a logical follow-on task order for the West Valley Demonstration Project (WVDP) for necessary technical, administrative, and database management services. The type of services are the same as the services described in the performance work statement for the master IDIQ contract, 89303322DEM000084, and currently being performed on the current WVDP TAC Task Order, 89303323FEM400321 (hereinafter the �Current WVDP TAC Task Order�). The proposed scope of the follow-on will also be initiated upon expiration of the period of performance of the current Task Order and the master IDIQ contract, and is well within the maximum ordering quantity of the master IDIQ contract. The current West Valley TAC Task Order was competitively awarded under the EM Field Site Technical Assistance Contracts (hereinafter �Site TACs�) Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract. Seven (7) contractors were awarded under the Site TACs IDIQ. The objective of the multiple award IDIQ is to provide technical assistance for DOE�s Field Sites supported by EMCBC. These sites include WVDP, EM Los Alamos Field Office (EM-LA), and the Moab Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action (UMTRA) Project, among other EM Field Sites. The scope of the Technical Assistance Contracts for EM Field Sites includes safeguards and security, emergency management, quality assurance, project integration, data management, administrative support, regulatory/environmental compliance, nuclear safety, waste management, records/information management, engineering, training, property management, public affairs, cost estimating, and technical editing. The Site TACs IDIQ has a five (5) year ordering period, with a period of performance from September 20, 2022 to September 19, 2027. Under the chosen IDIQ contract type, the authority exists to issue logical follow-on task orders. The FAR and the Site TACs IDIQ (H.41 Task Ordering Procedure) provide statutory and contractual exceptions to the Fair Opportunity process. Among these exceptions is the issuance of a Task Order on a sole-source basis in the interest of economy and efficiency as a logical follow-on to an order already issued under the IDIQ contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the original WVDP Task Order. All eligible EM Site TACs contract holders were provided a fair opportunity to compete for this work. Before issuance of the current WVDP TAC Task Order, all seven holders of Site TACs contracts were provided a Request for Task Order Proposal on November 4, 2022 with a requested proposal submission deadline of November 20, 2022. Six (6) contractors submitted proposals in response to the solicitation and FPM AECOM JV1 was selected. FPM AECOM JV1�s management approach and transition of work approach and capability combined with a realistic and reasonable cost and price resulted in the best value determination in its favor. The Ordering procedures of the Site TACs IDIQ (clause H.41) included statutory exceptions to the Fair Opportunity Process allowing DOE to issue a logical follow-on task order on a sole source basis in the interest of economy and efficiency. Thus, contract provisions put all eligible Site TACs IDIQ contractors on notice at the time the Current WVDP TAC Task Order was solicited that DOE could issue the awardee a sole-source logical follow-on task order. The Current WVDP TAC Task Order is valued at approximately $9M and the period of performance is from 1/23/2023 to 09/12/2026. Under the Current WVDP TAC Task Order, DOE is currently utilizing services related to project controls, safeguards and security, quality assurance, administrative support, and emergency management. FPM AECOM JV1�s performance in providing the required services to date has been rated Very Good to Exceptional, reflecting excellent quality, cost control and management. FPM AECOM JV1 has built effective working relationships with stakeholders and has been very flexible, able to respond quickly and positively to changes and direction from DOE. If DOE transitions to a new contractor, it can expect to experience increases in costs, quality variances and management risks during the time it would take for the new contractor to learn to perform at least as well as FPM AECOM JV1 is now performing. Additionally, DOE expends at least two years of time and resources when it procures such services competitively. Through its several years of high-quality performance, FPM AECOM JV1 has gained valuable institutional knowledge and experience to continue performing well. The work at the WVDP will benefit from moving forward towards a finished state rather than experiencing the delays and possible missteps or even dangers that would result from introducing a less experienced contractor to the project work. Consequently, DOE expects to achieve significant benefits in economy and efficiencies by issuing a logical follow-on task order to FPM AECOM JV1 for the WVDP TAC Task Order. Considering the benefits to the WVDP of continued performance by FPM AECOM JV1 and the costs in time and resources to re-compete the Task Order, issuing FPM AECOM JV1 a follow-on task order on a sole-source basis will be the most economic and efficient method to meet the requirements. The application of this contract, with the skillset listed above is the most efficient application of technical and administrative support requirements if/when DOE needs immediate support with highly competent and qualified individuals with the required expertise. IV. Authority Permitting a Fair Opportunity Exception FAR 16.505(b)(1)(i) requires the Contracting Officer to provide each awardee under a multiple award contract, a fair opportunity to be considered for each order exceeding the micro-purchase threshold ($15,000) unless a statutory exception applies. The specific exception that precludes the fair opportunity process for this acquisition is FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C): The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the interest of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued under the contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the original order. The new WVDP TAC Task Order is a logical follow-on in terms of the anticipated scope of the, period of performance, and value as all will be comparable to the current Task Order that FPM AECOM JV1 is successfully performing (see discussion in Sections III and VI). The IDIQ contracts offer DOE access to a pre-qualified pool of 12 Small Businesses and allow for streamlined task order awards. General Reason for Non-Selection: The award decision was IAW Solicitation FA930126Q0023 evaluation instructions and criteria, provided in the Addendum to RFO 52.212-1 and RFO 52.212-2. The award was made to the offeror within the competitive range whose response represented the best value, with non-price factors weighed more heavily than price. In the integrated assessment upon which the award will be made, the non-price factors of Technical Acceptability and Past Performance were to be weighed more heavily than Price. The nature of this service demands a contractor with proven expertise, and prioritizing price alone risks compromising health and safety. Past performance is also critical, as contractors with historical success with the performance requirements and who can operate independently offer significant efficiency gains. To arrive at a best value decision, the Government first evaluated responses for technical acceptability. For all technically acceptable responses, the Government then conducted a tradeoff analysis of Past Performance and Price in which award could be made to a higher-priced offeror if determined that the benefit of its superior past performance was worth the additional price, or an award would be made to a lower-priced offeror if their past performance was not considered to be worth a price premium.
